hypotheses.title: GEO has assembled a distributed ICE expertise channel across leadership, BI consulting, and lobbying
Former-official hiring, consulting, and lobbying are ordinary regulated-sector practices without a coordinated channel

findings.target_name: Matthew T. Albence
findings.summary: GEO disclosed that Matthew Albence previously held multiple ICE roles culminating as Acting Director.

findings.target_name: Daniel Ragsdale
findings.summary: GEO disclosed that Daniel Ragsdale served as ICE Deputy Director from 2012 to 2017.

findings.target_name: Julie Myers Wood
findings.summary: GEO disclosed that director Julie Myers Wood headed ICE from January 2006 through November 2008.

findings.target_name: Guidepost Solutions LLC
findings.summary: GEO disclosed that Guidepost Solutions, director Julie Myers Wood’s employer, had a consulting agreement with subsidiary B.I. Incorporated.

findings.target_name: Guidepost Solutions LLC
findings.summary: GEO disclosed that $420,000 was paid under the Guidepost-B.I. Incorporated consulting agreement for 2025.

findings.target_name: B.I. Incorporated
findings.summary: GAO reported that ICE does not fully assess the B.I. Incorporated contractor against performance standards established in the ISAP contract.

findings.target_name: The GEO Group, Inc.
findings.summary: GEO’s Q4 2025 LD-2 reported $340,000 and lobbying on ICE, immigration enforcement, and alternatives to detention.

findings.target_name: Checkmate Government Relations
findings.summary: Checkmate Government Relations reported $150,000 in Q4 2025 lobbying income from GEO for contracts related to detention centers.

findings.target_name: Guidepost Solutions LLC / B.I. Incorporated / Julie Myers Wood
findings.summary: GEO disclosed that the Guidepost-B.I. consulting agreement was already in place for fiscal 2013 before GEO appointed Guidepost CEO Julie Myers Wood to its board effective July 2, 2014.

findings.target_name: The GEO Group, Inc. Audit and Finance Committee / Guidepost-B.I. relationship
findings.summary: GEO stated that its Audit and Finance Committee reviewed and approved the related-party transactions disclosed alongside the Guidepost-B.I. consulting relationship.

findings.target_name: Matthew Albence / GrindStone Strategic Consulting LLC / The GEO Group, Inc.
findings.summary: GEO disclosed $137,531 paid to Matthew Albence’s GrindStone Strategic Consulting in 2022 for services provided before Albence joined GEO; GEO said GrindStone provided no services after he joined.

findings.target_name: Daniel Ragsdale / The GEO Group, Inc.
findings.summary: GEO states that Daniel Ragsdale joined the company in July 2017 as Executive Vice President for Contract Compliance and was promoted effective January 1, 2025.

findings.target_name: Checkmate Government Relations / The GEO Group, Inc.
findings.summary: Senate LDA filings place Checkmate’s GEO engagement from August 13, 2025 through May 4, 2026 and disclose $460,000 across the latest Q3 2025, Q4 2025, amended Q1 2026, and terminating Q2 2026 filings.

findings.target_name: Guidepost Solutions LLC / B.I. Incorporated
findings.summary: GEO’s 2026 proxy says the Guidepost-B.I. consulting agreement was not extended past December 31, 2025; the most recent monthly retainer was $35,000.

findings.target_name: BI Incorporated
findings.summary: Structured award records trace BI through ISAP I-V under full-and-open procedures; recorded parent-level offer counts were 3, 3, 4, 2, and 2, respectively.

findings.target_name: BI Incorporated
findings.summary: ICE separately awarded BI one of 14 prime IDIQs under the full-and-open 26-SOL-DCR-01 skip-tracing competition; BI records show 51 parent-level offers and a $1,624,500 first task order.

findings.target_name: BI Incorporated
findings.summary: Public structured data and the reviewed ISAP V package do not identify BI device manufacturers, commercial-data suppliers, or subcontractors; this is an unresolved supplier chain, not evidence that none exist.

findings.target_name: Thomas D. Homan / GEO Care / Guidepost Solutions
findings.summary: Thomas D. Homan’s certified 2025 executive-branch financial disclosure lists GEO Care and Guidepost Solutions as sources that paid more than $5,000 in a calendar year for consulting services during the reporting period.

findings.target_name: David J. Venturella / The GEO Group / U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
findings.summary: ICE's current leadership page identifies David J. Venturella as the official performing the duties of ICE director and states that he served as a GEO Group senior vice president from 2012 through 2023.

findings.target_name: Pamela Bondi / The GEO Group / Trump transition and administration
findings.summary: A Q3 2019 Senate LDA activity row listed Pamela Bondi among the Ballard lobbyists on GEO work and named DHS and the White House Office as contacted entities, but the activity-level fields do not attribute either entity contact to Bondi.

findings.target_name: Justin J. Sayfie / The GEO Group / Trump White House fellowships commission
findings.summary: A Senate LDA filing for Ballard Partners' GEO Group account named Justin J. Sayfie as a lobbyist and identified him as a White House Fellows commissioner; a Trump White House release had announced the president's intent to appoint Sayfie to that commission.

findings.target_name: Christopher LaCivita Jr. / Checkmate Government Relations / The GEO Group; Chris LaCivita / Trump campaign
findings.summary: Checkmate's August 2025 GEO Group registration named Christopher LaCivita Jr. as a lobbyist on detention-center contracts; its amended Q1 2026 report again named Jr. and listed the White House Office. Separately, Trump's campaign identified his father, Chris LaCivita, as a senior campaign adviser; finding #12710 documents that they are distinct people.

findings.target_name: Matthew Albence / Thomas Homan / Daniel Ragsdale / ICE Presidential Transition Office
findings.summary: An official ICE presidential-transition packet identifies Matthew Albence and Thomas Homan as subject-matter experts who cleared an ICE transition response and Daniel Ragsdale as the ICE approving official.

findings.target_name: Thomas D. Homan / Guidepost Solutions / B.I. Incorporated
findings.summary: GEO paid Guidepost $180,000 under its B.I. consulting agreement in each of fiscal 2023 and 2024, but no primary record reviewed ties Homan to that engagement; the common Guidepost appearance remains an unresolved second-degree connection.

findings.target_name: David J. Venturella
findings.summary: After retiring as GEO SVP on 2023-02-01, Venturella contracted through 2025-01-31 to help GEO submit proposals and renew contracts

findings.target_name: David J. Venturella / ICE procurement authority
findings.summary: ICE publicly places acquisition and procurement activities under Management and Administration; the current leadership page and a June 2026 APFS record do not assign Venturella an operational acquisition role.

findings.target_name: Checkmate Government Relations / The GEO Group / DHS detention actions
findings.summary: Checkmate's 265-day GEO engagement overlapped fewer DHS actions but greater net obligations than the equal prior window, while the same number of base actions and pre-engagement August awards prevent attributing the change to lobbying timing.

findings.target_name: David J. Venturella / The GEO Group / U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
findings.summary: Venturella first appeared on ICE's archived leadership page 472 days after his GEO proposal-support consultancy ended and 429 days after scheduled performance-share vesting, while public records still leave the exact ethics and participation boundary unresolved.

findings.target_name: Christopher LaCivita Jr. / Chris LaCivita identity distinction
findings.summary: The Checkmate lobbyist named in GEO disclosures is Christopher LaCivita Jr., the son of—not the same person as—Trump 2024 campaign adviser Chris LaCivita.

findings.target_name: Checkmate Government Relations / The GEO Group, Inc.
findings.summary: The complete Senate LDA series contains six filings: a 2025 registration, Q3 and Q4 reports, an original and amended Q1 2026 report, and a Q2 termination; counting only the latest Q1 amendment yields $460,000 and a May 4, 2026 termination date.

findings.target_name: Checkmate Government Relations / The GEO Group, Inc.
findings.summary: Every Checkmate-GEO activity disclosure used the same broad detention-contract wording; the disclosed contacted entities were the White House Office, HHS, BOP, and later ACF—not DHS or ICE—and no filing named a facility, PIID, solicitation, official, procurement milestone, or requested award outcome.

findings.target_name: Checkmate Government Relations / The GEO Group / ICE procurement
findings.summary: All detention-service base actions recorded during Checkmate’s August 13, 2025–May 4, 2026 engagement were orders or calls under parent vehicles established before the engagement; North Lake and South Texas annual base tasks were awarded 12 days and one day before it began.

findings.target_name: Trump administration detention-capacity policy / ICE funding
findings.summary: The January 20, 2025 detention-facilities order and the July 4, 2025 $45 billion ICE detention-capacity appropriation both predated Checkmate’s August 13 engagement, supplying a public policy-and-budget explanation for later detention obligations independent of an award-specific lobbying inference.

findings.target_name: Aurora Contract Detention Facility / DHS APFS F2026072762
findings.summary: DHS’s February 12, 2026 Aurora follow-on forecast identified GEO as incumbent, but placed the estimated solicitation release on June 1, 2026 and the anticipated award in Q4 FY2026—after Checkmate’s May 4 termination.

findings.target_name: Checkmate Government Relations / GEO public contact records
findings.summary: A bounded exact-name search of public White House, DHS, ICE, HHS, ACF, BOP, GAO, oversight, FOIA-library, MuckRock, and DocumentCloud materials located no calendar, visitor-log, correspondence, procurement-integrity, or ethics record tying a Checkmate-GEO lobbyist to a named detention procurement.

findings.target_name: Ballard Partners / The GEO Group / Pamela Bondi
findings.summary: The complete Senate LDA series contains 18 Ballard-GEO filings from a 2017-02-01 registration through a 2021-01-31 termination, reports $1.8 million in income, and shows Bondi only in 2019 Q3 before the Q4 filing removed her; the activity-level government-entity fields do not attribute a contact to Bondi or another named lobbyist.

findings.target_name: DHS / Ballard Partners
findings.summary: DHS reported that its Headquarters/Office of the Chief Information Officer located no responsive records in a search for political-appointee communications with named Ballard Partners personnel from 2017-01-20 through 2019-02-14.

findings.target_name: Daniel McFaul / Sylvester Lukis / OMB
findings.summary: Official OMB visitor files record three appointment groups involving Ballard GEO-roster lobbyists in 2018-2019, but the records identify no client or purpose and cannot be attributed to GEO, ICE, DHS, or a procurement.

findings.target_name: The GEO Group / Department of Homeland Security direct-prime procurement universe
findings.summary: After exact-key removal of parent/child overlaps, the normalized 14-UEI GEO universe contains 1,416 unique DHS prime-contract action rows across 222 award PIIDs and $6,356,699,228.62 in net action obligations from 2015-01-01 through 2026-07-13; ICE accounts for 1,362 actions/212 awards/$6,354,097,259.08 and CBP for 54 actions/10 awards/$2,601,969.54.

findings.target_name: GEO DHS prime-contract action timing by presidential administration
findings.summary: Within the corrected 2015–2026 action ledger, ICE net action obligations were $478,295,618.46 before Trump I, $1,686,365,164.41 during Trump I, $2,900,292,455.05 during Biden, and $1,289,144,021.16 during Trump II through 2026-07-13; CBP totals for those periods were $458,026.46, $852,954.45, $934,664.66, and $356,323.97.

findings.target_name: The GEO Group / DHS contract action pace by administration
findings.summary: Duration-normalized DHS GEO action frequency is only 7.3% higher in Trump II than Trump I through 2026-07-13, while net obligation pace is 106.8% higher because average obligation per action nearly doubled.
